Take the extreme viewpoint, the programme "naked and afraid" has contestants surviving on very little food for 21 days for a survival challenge. They do suffer but I reckon it takes a good week before the effects of no food really start kicking in.

For long duration starvation challenges, it's often times much much worse if you eat small amounts of food throughout the challenge -- especially if they are carbs/simple sugars. It's actually better to not eat anything at all.

I've done a 30 day water-only fast and it was actually fairly easy. After a few days without food, your body goes into ketosis and becomes fat adapted -- the brain switches fuel from glucose to the ketone betahydroxybutyrate. Hunger pretty much completely disappears. If you eat above a certain threshold of net carbs, you'll get kicked out ketosis and the brain will start sending hunger signals again. If one ever find oneself in a food shortage, it's way better to just not eat than to live off rice, canned food, or even worse, vending machine food. That's just asking to have a bad time. In a true food shortage, it actually does make sense to consume a stick of butter or a block of cheese, since fat has a higher energy density and is the optimal method our body prefers for carrying fuel for a prolonged period of time/distance.
